note: SPEED step 3: what the project's own infrastructure measured, read-only (SELECT on the production database and the Supabase log stream through the connector, 2026-09-26 22:50 → 2026-09-27 01:10 UTC), plus the documented limits. Each figure carries the query or page it came from.

settings.cron.use_background_workers: off (each run opens a connection to localhost)

every_minute_jobs.query: select jobid, count(*), percentile_cont(.5|.9) within group (order by extract(epoch from start_time - date_trunc('minute', start_time))), percentile_cont(.5|.99) within group (order by extract(epoch from end_time - start_time)) from cron.job_run_details where start_time > now() - interval '6 hours' and jobid in (16,18,19,24,25) group by jobid

documented.schedule: every second to once a year (Supabase Cron guide); '1 seconds' .. '59 seconds'
documented.advice: no more than 8 jobs running concurrently; each job no more than 10 minutes (supabase.com/docs/guides/cron)

pg_net.documented: intended for at most 200 requests a second; responses kept 6 hours (supabase.com/docs/guides/database/extensions/pg_net)

invocations_24h_to_2026-09-27T01:00Z.note: jobs 24 (books) and 25 (pmrw-e) started inside this window; with all five every-minute jobs running a full day the cron share is ~7,900 a day
invocations_24h_to_2026-09-27T01:00Z.query: select log_attributes['request.pathname'], count(*) from logs where source = 'function_edge_logs' group by 1

plan_quota.over: $2 per 1 million, billed in whole packages (supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/edge-function-invocations)

pg_net_invoked_start_after_minute_ms.query: quantile(.5|.9)((toUnixTimestamp64Milli(timestamp) - execution_time_ms) % 60000) from function_edge_logs where user_agent like 'pg_net%' group by request.search

cpu_ms_per_call.source: function_logs Shutdown events' cpu_time_used joined to function_edge_logs by execution_id, 6 h to 2026-09-26 22:50 UTC

cloudflare_documented.workers_paid: $5 a month minimum; 10 million requests and 30 million CPU ms included, then $0.30 a million and $0.02 a million CPU ms; CPU 30 s a request by default, up to 5 minutes; 10,000 subrequests an invocation by default (up to 10 million, since 2026-02-11); six connections waiting for headers at once, outbound WebSockets included (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing, /limits)
cloudflare_documented.durable_objects_paid: requests 1 million a month included then $0.15 a million (HTTP, RPC, WebSocket messages at 20:1, alarm invocations); duration 400,000 GB-s a month included then $12.50 a million GB-s, billed at 128 MB while the object is in memory and cannot hibernate; CPU 30 s a request by default, configurable to 5 minutes; alarm handler wall time 15 minutes; 6 simultaneous outbound connections; soft limit 1,000 requests a second an object (developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing, /limits)
cloudflare_documented.outbound_websocket: an outbound WebSocket or connect() socket keeps the object alive (and billed for duration) for at most 15 minutes a connection, after which the 70-140 s eviction rule resumes; outgoing WebSockets do not hibernate (changelog 2026-06-19; /durable-objects/concepts/durable-object-lifecycle)
cloudflare_documented.alarms: setAlarm() at millisecond precision, one alarm at a time, re-armed by the handler; at-least-once, retried with backoff from 2 s up to six times (/durable-objects/api/alarms, /api/base)
cloudflare_documented.placement: location hints (wnam, enam, weur, eeur, apac, oc, ...) are best effort; jurisdictions guarantee the EU or the US, not a country (/durable-objects/reference/data-location)
cloudflare_documented.cron_triggers: Workers Cron Triggers run at most once a minute; a sub-minute clock is an alarm
cloudflare_documented.account: the connector lists two unrelated Workers on the account (ride-a-stock, football-career); its plan is not shown by the read-only tools
